meta.title: Palette
meta.description: A visual color palette editor with a 2D HSV picker, sortable swatches, and one-click export to hex arrays, CSS custom properties, Tailwind config, or HSL strings.

blocks.content: Color palettes live at the boundary between design and code. The designer picks colors. The developer needs them as CSS custom properties, a Tailwind config object, or a JSON array. Most handoff flows produce one format and leave the conversion to the developer. The Palette system covers both ends: a visual swatch editor with a 2D picker, and an export panel that outputs the exact format your codebase expects.

Colors are stored as lowercase hex strings internally. The 2D picker operates in HSV space — saturation on the x-axis, brightness on the y-axis — because HSV maps cleanly to the canvas gradient axes. All format conversions (to HSL, RGB, or tailwind tokens) happen at the export boundary. The swatch grid uses the Sortable system internally, so drag-to-reorder works out of the box.

blocks.title: Default new color
blocks.content: The Add button seeds new swatches with #c2f13c. Override by calling add(hex) from usePalette with your own starting hex — useful for pre-loading a brand color when the palette first opens.
Click a swatch to select it. Double-click or click Edit to open the color editor. Drag the grip icon to reorder. Use Export to copy the palette in any format.
Palette depends on the Sortable system for swatch reordering. Install Sortable first if you haven't already.

steps.title: Install Sortable peer dependencies
steps.description: Palette's swatch grid uses Sortable internally.

blocks.content: Drop PaletteRoot anywhere. The default layout renders the toolbar, swatch grid, and color editor automatically. Pass defaultColors to seed it with existing swatches.

Pass colors + onChange to take full control of the color array. Every mutation — add, edit, remove, reorder — calls onChange with the complete updated array. Use this when the palette feeds a form, a theme config, or any external state.

blocks.title: Internal state is bypassed in controlled mode
blocks.content: When colors is provided, the component does not maintain its own array. Your onChange handler must update state and pass the new array back as colors. If you return the same reference, mutations will appear to have no effect.
The Export button in the toolbar generates the palette in four formats. Named colors use kebab-case derived from the name field. Unnamed colors fall back to color-1, color-2, etc.

blocks.filename: Sample output for Lime / Slate 950 / Slate 50

blocks.content: Pass children to PaletteRoot to replace the default layout entirely. All composable parts — PaletteGrid, PaletteColorEditor, PaletteToolbar — are available individually and use the same context.

blocks.title: PaletteColorEditor mounts conditionally
blocks.content: PaletteColorEditor renders nothing when editingId is null. You can always include it in your layout — it appears only when the user opens a swatch for editing, and disappears when they close it.

usePalette exposes the full context anywhere inside PaletteRoot. Use it to build custom toolbar buttons, wire palette state into a form, sync to an external store, or trigger actions from outside the default UI.
